(def seq-reduce
  (fn ([f coll]
    (if-let [s (seq coll)]
      (reduce f (first s) (next s))
      (f)))
  ([f val coll]
    ;; A chunked seq reduces a chunk at a time, as Clojure's InternalReduce
    ;; does, rather than allocating a seq per element (#446). A chunk's
    ;; elements are read by index to its count: a filter's chunk is shorter
    ;; than its array. A reduced value ends the reduction.
    (loop [val val, coll (seq coll)]
      (if coll
        (if (chunked-seq? coll)
          (let [c (chunk-first coll)
                n (suss.bootstrap/long-cast (-count c))
                ^objects input-array (suss.bootstrap/chunk-array c)
                input-offset (if (suss.bootstrap/undefined? input-array)
                                     0
                                     (suss.bootstrap/long-cast (suss.bootstrap/chunk-offset c)))
                nval (loop [i 0 val val]
                       (if (< i n)
                         (let [nval (f val (if (suss.bootstrap/undefined? input-array)
                                              (-nth c i)
                                              (aget input-array (+ input-offset i))))]
                           (if (reduced? nval)
                             nval
                             (recur (inc i) nval)))
                         val))]
            (if (reduced? nval)
              @nval
              (recur nval (seq (chunk-rest coll)))))
          (let [nval (f val (first coll))]
            (if (reduced? nval)
              @nval
              (recur nval (next coll)))))
        val)))))

A chunked seq's 3-arity reduction reads each chunk by index, as Clojure's InternalReduce for chunked seqs does, with reduced termination and source order kept (#446). A canonical well-formed Object[] chunk admits a loop-invariant typed storage view and immutable offset. Each element is still read immediately before its reducer call; custom chunks and unsupported windows/storage keep the original indexed protocol call. Widen the ICounted int result once to a raw long local, preserving reduced short-circuiting and chunk-boundary realization. Numeric local metadata alone does not insert a physical conversion. Use explicit inline long casts for the ICounted result and admitted immutable offset, and for str loop state read back from its temporary pair, so the IR carries raw longs through arithmetic/array indexing without adding a primitive function entry. Early core definitions precede the public long var; the private long-cast word emits the same existing checked LongCast operation.
